source.citation: Dahut et al., J Clin Pharmacol (2009), 49:650–660
source.location: Table 6, population mean column; clearance row for the normal renal function group
source.population_context: Adult Phase I advanced solid-tumor population; not a myeloma-derived model. The study enrolled 45 participants, predominantly with prostate cancer.
source.scope: Four published central parameter estimates only; no patient covariate equation or variability model is implemented.

apparent_clearance_ml_min.basis: Published central estimate for the normal renal function group; fixed reference, not assigned from eGFR.

assumptions: One compartment; first-order absorption and elimination; a single invented oral dose at time zero.
Use apparent CL/F and V/F directly. Absolute bioavailability is not estimated or multiplied into the concentration again.
All reference parameters are fixed. Age, sex, weight, eGFR, medication names and indication do not select or alter them.
Comparison scales clearance alone by an explicitly chosen 0.5, 1 or 2; these values are mathematical experiments, not clinical categories.
No repeat dosing, accumulation, treatment cycles, meals, active metabolites, between-person variability or residual error.
Accept 5–40 mg inputs as a boundary matching the study dose span, not as a suggested regimen. No mg/kg or mg/m² conversion.

equations.concentration: C(time) = 1000 × dose/(V/F) × ka/(ka − ke) × [exp(−ke × u) − exp(−ka × u)], in ng/mL
